title: Gap-down bounce
about: Buy Nifty 50 stocks that open 3% or more below yesterday's close, and sell them at 3:15 the same day.

lines.universe: Nifty 50 stocks as the index stood on each day, including ones later dropped
lines.data: One-minute bars and best bid and offer from NSE, adjusted for splits and bonuses, with bad prints filtered out
lines.trading: Buys at 9:20, once the gap is known, at the 9:20 offer
lines.costs: Brokerage, STT, exchange fees, stamp duty and GST, plus 5 bps slippage each way
lines.testing: Rule taken as it is from a 2015 paper and run once on 2016–2024, with no tuning
lines.result: 1,240 trades over nine years, judged against the Nifty's move over the same hours

cases.line: Today's 50 Nifty stocks, run back to 2016
cases.why: Today's Nifty 50 is a list of survivors. Stocks that kept falling and were dropped from the index aren't in the test, so it never buys a gap-down that turned into a collapse.

cases.line: Buys at the day's low, once the gap is known
cases.why: Nobody knows the day's low until the close. Buying at the low every time uses the future, which is why the result looks so smooth.

cases.line: ₹20 brokerage an order, and nothing else
cases.why: Brokerage is the smallest cost. STT, exchange fees, stamp duty and slippage on 1,240 intraday round trips can add up to more than the edge.

cases.line: Last trades as received, with bad prints left in
cases.why: One bad print far below the market looks like a deep gap and a cheap fill. The test books a profit on a price nobody could have traded at.

title: Twelve-month momentum
about: Each month, hold the 30 Nifty 500 stocks with the best returns over the past year, skipping the latest month.

lines.universe: Nifty 500 members as on each rebalance date, delisted stocks included
lines.data: Month-end closes adjusted for splits, bonuses and dividends
lines.trading: Ranks on the month-end close and buys at the next day's open
lines.costs: 0.2% a side for brokerage, taxes and impact, on the trades it really makes
lines.testing: Lookback and skip month set by the textbook rule, then tested once on 2010–2024
lines.result: Long only, so it is judged against the Nifty 500, after costs

cases.line: Stocks in the Nifty 500 today, traced back to 2010
cases.why: Some of momentum's worst trades are past winners that later collapsed and left the index. Testing only today's members leaves those losses out.

cases.line: Up 26% a year, against 7% for fixed deposits; long only, with a beta of 1.2 to Nifty
cases.why: A long-only book with a beta of 1.2 rides the market. The fair test is against the Nifty 500, which also rose a lot; only what's left after that is edge.

cases.line: The best of 60 ranking ideas the team tried on 2010–2024
cases.why: Try 60 ideas on the same years and the best one will look good by luck alone. Its Sharpe needs deflating for the 60 tries, and it needs a test on fresh data.

title: Results drift
about: Buy stocks whose quarterly profit beats analysts' estimates by 10% or more, and hold them for 20 trading days.

lines.universe: All NSE stocks with analyst coverage at the time, including ones later delisted
lines.data: Results and estimates time-stamped to the minute they were published
lines.trading: Buys at the next open after the results come out
lines.costs: Costs and slippage scaled to each stock's trading volume
lines.testing: Thresholds chosen on 2012–2018, then tested once on 2019–2024
lines.result: 2,900 trades over 12 years, hedged with Nifty futures

cases.line: Results dated to the last day of the quarter they cover
cases.why: Companies have up to 45 days after a quarter ends to publish results, and 60 for the full year. Dating them to the quarter end lets the test trade weeks before anyone knew.

cases.line: Works with a 20-day hold; at 15 or 25 days it loses money
cases.why: A real effect works across nearby settings. A result that lives at one exact holding period is most likely fitted to the noise in this history.

cases.line: Fills at the opening price with no slippage, even in small caps
cases.why: Small caps have wide spreads, and buying them moves the price. Over 2,900 trades, free fills can turn a loss into a profit on paper.

cases.line: Stocks still listed today that have analyst coverage
cases.why: Firms delisted after frauds or failures are missing. Some beat estimates just before they collapsed, and those losses never show up.

title: Expiry-day short straddle
about: Sell the at-the-money Nifty call and put at 9:30 on expiry day, and buy them back by 3:15.

lines.universe: Nifty weekly options, on expiry days only
lines.data: Option quotes for each minute: the bid and the ask, not just last trades
lines.trading: Sells at the 9:30 bid; stop-losses fill at the next minute's ask
lines.costs: Brokerage, STT on the premium sold, exchange fees and GST, plus the bid-ask spread
lines.testing: Entry time and stop fixed in advance from desk practice, with no tuning
lines.result: 190 expiries since 2021, the worst ones included, with margin counted in the return

cases.line: No costs, and fills at the last traded price
cases.why: Selling at the last trade ignores the bid-ask spread, which on expiry day is a real share of the premium collected. Add STT, fees and GST and the edge may be gone.

cases.line: Sells at 9:47 with a 23% stop; at 9:45 or with a 25% stop it loses
cases.why: A knife-edge result. If two minutes or two points of stop flip it to a loss, the test has found the noise of these particular days, not an edge.

cases.line: Picks the strike nearest where Nifty closes that day
cases.why: At 9:30 nobody knows where Nifty will close. Choosing the strike it ends nearest makes the straddle look far safer than it is.

cases.line: Built on the last 30 expiries, all in a quiet market
cases.why: Thirty calm expiries say little about a trade that loses big on rare wild days. A short option book needs years that include the shocks.

title: Two-bank pairs trade
about: Trade the gap between two large private banks: sell the dear one and buy the cheap one when the gap stretches.

lines.universe: One pair, chosen for business reasons before looking at any prices
lines.data: Z-score from the past 60 days only, recomputed each day
lines.trading: Signal at the close; both legs fill at the next open
lines.costs: Costs on both legs, plus rolling the short futures leg each month
lines.testing: Entry, exit and stop rules fixed in advance; tested once on 2014–2024
lines.result: 64 trades over ten years, with equal rupee legs so market moves mostly cancel

cases.line: Z-score uses the average and spread of the whole 2014–2024 period
cases.why: In 2016 you couldn't know the average gap over the next eight years. Using it tells the test where the spread will settle, so every trade seems to snap back.

cases.line: Nine trades over ten years, with equal rupee legs
cases.why: Nine trades is far too few to tell skill from luck. A couple of lucky exits could be the whole result.

cases.line: Costs on the cash leg only; the futures leg and its monthly roll are free
cases.why: The short side sits in futures, which cost brokerage, fees and a roll every month. Leaving them out flatters a trade that earns only a little per round trip.

cases.line: The best pair out of 2,000 tried on the same years
cases.why: Scan 2,000 pairs and some will have mean-reverted beautifully by luck. The winner needs a fresh test on years it wasn't picked from.

title: Small-cap bounce
about: Each week, buy the 20 small caps that fell most in the past week, and sell them a week later.

lines.universe: Nifty Smallcap 250 members on each date, including ones later delisted
lines.data: Volume-weighted prices; stocks that didn't trade that week are skipped
lines.trading: Signal on Friday's close; buys spread over Monday's session
lines.costs: Costs plus market impact sized to each stock's daily volume
lines.testing: One-week hold set before the test; run once on 2012–2024
lines.result: Judged against the Nifty Smallcap 250 index, after costs

cases.line: Last traded prices, including stocks that trade only a few times a week
cases.why: A stock that didn't trade keeps its old price, then jumps when it does. The test sees fake drops and fake bounces, and books profits no one could have taken.

cases.line: ₹5 crore a week, assumed to trade with no market impact
cases.why: ₹5 crore a week in thin small caps would move prices a long way. Without impact costs, the test assumes fills that don't exist.

cases.line: Small caps still listed today
cases.why: Small caps that kept falling and were delisted are exactly what a buy-the-losers rule buys. Leaving them out removes its worst trades.

cases.line: Up 34% a year, against 7% for fixed deposits; long only
cases.why: Small caps rallied hard over these years. A long-only small-cap book should be judged against the small-cap index, not deposits; much of this may be the market.

title: Short the frothiest stocks
about: Each month, short stock futures on the 10 F&O stocks that rose most over the past year, hedged with Nifty futures.

lines.universe: F&O stocks as listed on each date, including ones later removed
lines.data: Prices adjusted for splits, bonuses and dividends
lines.trading: Signal on the month-end close; shorts at the next open
lines.costs: Costs on both sides, plus rolling the futures each month
lines.testing: One rule, taken from a research note; tested once on 2012–2024
lines.result: 1,400 trades over 12 years, with beta near zero after the Nifty hedge

cases.line: Prices as printed, not adjusted for splits or bonuses
cases.why: Big winners often announce a split or a bonus. On that day the unadjusted price halves, and the test counts a 50% gain on the short that never happened.

cases.line: Brokerage only: no STT, no roll costs and no slippage on 1,400 trades
cases.why: Each trade pays STT and fees, and every short future is rolled monthly. On 1,400 trades, leaving those out can be the whole profit.

cases.line: Eight settings, tuned on 2012–2024 and shown on 2012–2024
cases.why: With eight knobs tuned on the very years it's shown on, the test has learnt this history. There are no unseen years left to check it on.

cases.line: The one short idea that worked, out of 85 the team tried
cases.why: After 85 tries, one is bound to look good by chance. Count the tries: deflate the Sharpe, then test it on new data.

title: Event-day straddle
about: Buy the at-the-money Nifty straddle the day before the Budget or an RBI policy, and sell it the day after.

lines.universe: Every Budget and RBI policy day since 2016, none left out
lines.data: Option quotes at the close: the bid and the ask, not last trades
lines.trading: Buys at the closing offer the day before; sells at the closing bid the day after
lines.costs: Brokerage, STT, fees and GST, plus the full bid-ask spread
lines.testing: Rule fixed in advance; there are no settings to tune
lines.result: 62 events over nine years, the losing ones shown too

cases.line: 62 events, but three huge Budget-day moves make all the profit
cases.why: Take away three days and nothing is left. A result that hangs on a handful of trades is a small sample, whatever the trade count says.

cases.line: Budget and RBI days since 2016, except ones where Nifty barely moved the next day
cases.why: Dropping the quiet days uses the outcome to pick the trades. Live, you buy the straddle before you know whether the day will be quiet.

cases.line: Buys and sells at the last traded price, paying brokerage only
cases.why: Around big events the bid-ask spread on options widens. Paying it twice per trade, plus STT and fees, takes a large bite out of a long straddle.

cases.line: Picked after testing straddles, strangles and spreads on 40 kinds of events
cases.why: Test enough structures on enough events and one will shine by luck. The winner of a big search needs its Sharpe deflated and a fresh test.

title: Sector rotation
about: Each month, hold the three Nifty sector indices with the best six-month returns, through a basket of each index's stocks.

lines.universe: Only the Nifty sector indices that existed and traded on each date
lines.data: Total-return indices, so dividends are counted
lines.trading: Ranks on the month-end close; switches at the next day's close
lines.costs: Spreads, brokerage and tax on each switch
lines.testing: Six-month lookback set before looking; tested once on 2008–2024
lines.result: Judged against Nifty, which it tracks with a beta of 1.0

cases.line: Up 19% a year against 6% for cash, with a beta of 1.1 to Nifty
cases.why: A fully invested sector book is mostly the market. Nifty itself did well over these years; the edge is only what's left after comparing with it.

cases.line: Works with a seven-month lookback; at six or eight months it trails Nifty
cases.why: When the neighbours of the chosen setting fail, the setting has been fitted to this history. A real effect doesn't vanish when you nudge it.

cases.line: The best of 150 lookback and holding mixes tried on 2008–2024
cases.why: With 150 tries on the same years, the best is bound to look good. Deflate its Sharpe for the tries, and test it on years it never saw.

cases.line: Includes indices launched since 2015, using their back-filled history
cases.why: New indices are often launched after a sector has done well, with history worked out backwards. That past was never tradable, and it flatters the sectors that made the cut.

title: Top fund picker
about: Every April, move into the five small-cap mutual funds with the best returns over the past year.

lines.universe: Every small-cap fund that existed each April, including ones later merged or closed
lines.data: Direct-plan NAVs, which already take out each fund's expense ratio
lines.trading: Ranks on the March NAVs; switches at the first April NAV
lines.costs: Exit loads and capital gains tax on each switch
lines.testing: One rule, with no settings; tested once on 2014–2024
lines.result: Judged against the Nifty Smallcap 250 index, after costs

cases.line: Small-cap funds that still exist today
cases.why: Funds that were merged or closed, often after poor years, are missing. Many disappeared in the mergers after SEBI's 2018 recategorisation. Testing only today's funds leaves out the losers.

cases.line: Up 24% a year, against 7% for fixed deposits
cases.why: Small-cap funds are almost all market. Compared with the small-cap index instead of deposits, most of this return would disappear.

cases.line: Every switch is free: no tax on the gains
cases.why: Each April switch sells at a profit, and gains above the yearly exemption are taxed. Paying that every year is a real drag that the test leaves out.

title: Opening range breakout
about: Buy Nifty futures if they break above the first 15 minutes' high, sell if they break below its low, and exit by 3:15.

lines.universe: Nifty futures, rolled to the next month two days before expiry
lines.data: One-minute bars from NSE, checked for bad ticks
lines.trading: Enters on the first one-minute close past the range, at the next minute's price
lines.costs: Brokerage, STT, fees and one tick of slippage each way
lines.testing: Range length set from desk practice; tested once on 2015–2024
lines.result: 2,100 trades over ten years, with the losing streaks shown

cases.line: Enters on the break, with its stop set at the day's low
cases.why: The day's low isn't known until the close. A stop placed there is never hit, which no live trade can promise.

cases.line: No slippage: fills at the exact breakout price
cases.why: Breakouts happen while the price is running, so fills come a tick or two worse. Over 2,100 trades, a missing tick each way is a big share of the profit.

cases.line: Eleven settings tuned on 2015–2024, from range length to weekday, month and VIX filters
cases.why: Eleven knobs can fit almost any history. Tuned and shown on the same years, the result says more about the tuning than the market.

cases.line: A VIX filter leaves 16 trades over ten years
cases.why: Sixteen trades can't tell an edge from luck. The filter has probably just kept the lucky days.

cases.line: Raw ticks, with bad prints and the odd zero price left in
cases.why: A single bad tick far from the market can 'break' the range and fill the entry at an impossible price. The test books those fake trades as profits.
